positions.text: MeritRank qualifies Kaal's architectural response to cheap Sybil identity creation. Nasrulin, Ishmaev, and Pouwelse model reputation as accumulated feedback on real contributions and experimentally show that transitivity and connectivity decay can bound the gain from additional Sybil identities. The fit is partial and cautionary: the study concerns MakerDAO feedback graphs rather than staked AI-agent validation pools, does not establish non-zero exit cost or attacker-independent pool composition, and finds that naive epoch decay can worsen Sybil tolerance by favoring fresh feedback.
scope_conditions: The response is limited to the full-text passages and the one mapped Kaal claim.
External evidence level: peer-reviewed BRAINS 2022 paper with full corresponding preprint, Crossref/OpenAlex/Semantic Scholar identity, version, independence, and non-retraction verification.
Mapping review tier: independent substantive scholarly-growth qualification.
MeritRank evaluates participant feedback in MakerDAO rather than autonomous AI-agent validation pools.
It does not test stake locking, non-zero exit cost, or attacker-independent pool composition.
Its effective transitivity and connectivity decays are graph-topology mechanisms, not inactivity-based reputation decay.
The paper reports that naive epoch decay can worsen Sybil tolerance by favoring fresh feedback, materially qualifying Kaal's broader decay proposition.
The evidence-bearing full text is the 2022 arXiv v1 preprint corresponding to the independently verified peer-reviewed BRAINS 2022 publication.
